scenarios.title: Prepare a bonded VLAN uplink for a NIC failure
scenarios.summary: One active-backup bond carries two VLANs. Repair its saved controller/member dependencies and prove that either NIC can carry both networks after startup.
scenarios.objective: Prepare bond0 and its member profiles for the next simulated startup so Reports and Audit can reach their supplied peers when both NICs are available, when enp1s0 is unavailable, and when enp2s0 is unavailable. Preserve the current bond configuration, attached membership and current Reports/Audit settings while re-reading the saved files; future success is not a current reconfiguration. Keep audit.nmconnection unchanged and keep audit0 without a default route. Retain all five supplied filenames and UUIDs. Choose Test startup profiles and inspect the results of all three cases.

steps: Inspect the saved controller, port and VLAN profiles, make the dependency repair, then check all three startup cases while preserving current settings.
scenarios.explanation: The controller must start matching bound ports. autoconnect-ports=1 starts those ports even when their own autoconnect is false; an unbound Ethernet profile does not join the bond. With both NIC profiles bound, active-backup uses the configured primary when available and the other member when the primary lacks carrier. Each selected member must carry the actual VLAN tag both ways. Saved-file changes and current selections are checked separately.
hints: Inspect autoconnect-ports in bond.nmconnection and compare controller/port-type in the two port files. Their own autoconnect=false does not prevent the controller from starting a matching port.
A profile without controller and port-type is an unbound Ethernet candidate. It cannot act as this bond’s backup merely because its cable has carrier.
scenarios.simplifications: Source-enabled bounded NetworkManager keyfile and settled active-backup projection, not a daemon/kernel or boot experiment. One supplied controller, two candidate NIC profiles, two manual IPv4 VLAN profiles and three fixed physical cases. Explicit miimon=100, primary_reselect=always/0, literal controller/parent names, 802.1Q and supplied VLAN flags1. No real timers, activation ordering, link negotiation, gratuitous ARP/MAC updates, packet timing, other bond modes, general nmcli/ip, independent port-driven startup/discovery, bridge, DHCP/IPv6 bond, nested controllers, host profiles/services/interfaces or network operations. Bound port IP groups may be omitted; unbound/controller methods are disabled. Current source-held snapshots stay distinct from edited future policy. Correct IP routes and both-direction tags are required; carrier alone is insufficient.
